test.name: Decline to declare exhaustive when key record types unsearched
test.description: q_001 in flynn-census-exhausted has its first plan completed (census + death cert) but probate records for Thomas Flynn have not been searched, and post-1860 censuses haven't been examined. The skill must NOT declare exhaustive — it should keep `stopped_because: null` and name the specific unsearched record types as the blocker. Tests the honesty-over-completion bias.

input.delegation:
Assess whether question q_001 is reasonably exhaustive and record the outcome — declaring if the criteria are met, and recording the decline if they are not.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: A decline here WRITES the stop (step mode, section B): every item on the active plan is closed and unsearched sources remain, so `q_001.search_stop.stopped_because` becomes `resources_spent` with `stop_criteria: null`, `status` left `in_progress`, and `not_reached` carrying a `deferred` entry per never-planned source. Writing nothing is the failure now; it used to be the requirement.
`justification` must open with the verdict — `Overturn risk: low` or `Overturn risk: high — <sources>`. That prefix is what the ladder reads to pick the default, so free prose without it is a miss.
`log_entry_ids` must list the log entries of EVERY plan of the question, not just the active one: both pl_001 and pl_002 here.

Should name at least one specific unsearched record type that bears on the parentage question (probate records, post-1860 censuses, naturalization papers, or Irish emigration manifests are all reasonable)
Should reference the existing q_002 declaration only as background, not as the basis for declaring q_001 exhaustive — the two questions are scoped differently
Tool Arguments: This is a decline/review response — Claude is not expected to call validate_research_schema.
